title: 2007 AMC 12B Problem 8
statement: Tom’s age is \(T\) years, which is also the sum of the ages of his three children. His age \(N\) years ago was twice the sum of their ages then. What is \(\frac{T}{N}?\)

solutions.text:
Tom’s age \(N\) years ago was \(T-N.\) His three children were each \(N\) years younger, so their ages then totaled \(T-3N.\)

The condition gives \[ T-N=2(T-3N), \] so \(5N=T\) and \(\frac{T}{N}=5.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: \(N\) years ago Tom was \(T-N;\) each child was \(N\) years younger
